process_area.title: Diversion, Disposal, Settlement & Site Cleanup Analytics

value_stream.name: Customer Construction Debris, Demolition Waste & Site Cleanup Operations

fields.Participants: Finance (VS-15/VS-17), Site Cleanup Coordinator, Hauler/Disposer (W5447), Revenue Assurance (VS-118)
fields.Trigger: Job completion + customer sign-off (W5455); monthly billing cycle

workflows.name: Job Settlement, Container Demurrage & Scrap/Rebate Recovery Billing

Automation Opportunity: - Estimate-vs-actuals auto-reconciliation; demurrage auto-billing from container telematics; scrap/rebate auto-credit capture.
Controls: - CTL-805 (ensure controlled execution — Diversion, Disposal, Settlement & Site Cleanup Analytics (PA-191.3).); CTL-114 (ensure PFRS 15 recognition & cut-off control); CTL-14 (ensure AP invoices match PO and GR); operational: scrap/rebate credits captured against cost of service.
Cross-references: - links to VS-15 (AP/billing), VS-17 (GL), VS-157 (revenue recognition), VS-118 (revenue assurance), VS-11 (project billing)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-leak risk**: under-billed demurrage/overruns or un-captured scrap/rebate credits leak margin; mitigated by reconciliation-against-actuals and revenue-assurance monitoring (VS-118).
- **Mis-recognition risk**: recognizing recovery credits as revenue rather than cost-offset distorts PFRS 15; mitigated by the accounting policy (VS-157).
System Touchpoints: - Work-order/billing (VS-15/VS-11); AP 3-way match (VS-15 W7); revenue recognition (VS-157); weight-ticket/manifest (W5451/W5452); revenue assurance (VS-118).

steps.activity: Reconcile the actual job: volume/weight hauled (W5451), streams routed (W5453), crew-hours, container dwell, and any change orders (W5454) vs the booked estimate (W5448).
Compute the final price (base service + per-cu.m/per-tonne hauling + container demurrage if over-dwell − scrap/rebate recovery credits).
Recognize revenue per PFRS 15 at completion (VS-157/W5448); book recovery/scrap credits against cost of service.
Settle vendor invoices (hauler/disposer) with 3-way match against manifests/weight tickets (VS-15 W7); capture demurrage/rebates accurately.
Resolve exceptions (overruns, disputed weights, vendor overcharge) and feed into revenue assurance (VS-118) and pricing health (W5464).

fields.Frequency: Per job invoice; weekly aging review
fields.Participants: Finance (VS-15/VS-16), Customer Service (VS-13), Site Cleanup Coordinator, customer
fields.Trigger: Settlement (W5457); billing cycle; customer dispute; aging

Automation Opportunity: - Evidence-auto-attach to invoices; dispute workflow with evidence; automated dunning; project-billing integration.
Controls: - CTL-21: invoicing accuracy/evidence; CTL-31 (credit-note control); CTL-23 (dispute/fraud guard); operational: every cleanup invoice carries manifest + sign-off evidence.
Cross-references: - links to VS-16 (AR/collections/disputes), VS-15 (billing), VS-68 (credit risk), VS-13 (customer service), VS-118 (revenue assurance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Evidence-less-dispute risk**: a customer disputes a hauling fee and BuildRight lacks the weight ticket/sign-off to defend it, forcing a write-off; mitigated by mandatory evidence attachment to every invoice.
- **B2B-collection-aging risk**: B2B project cleanup invoices age with the broader project receivable; mitigated by VS-16 collection discipline and VS-68 credit risk.
System Touchpoints: - AR/invoicing (VS-16); billing evidence store (manifests/photos); dispute/credit-note (VS-16); collections/aging (VS-16); CRM (VS-13).
Time Estimate: - ~5–10 min/invoice generation; dispute resolution varies; ~1–2 hours/week aging review.

steps.activity: Generate and deliver the customer invoice with the manifest/weight evidence and before/after photos attached for transparency.
For B2B projects, integrate with progress billing (VS-11 W165/W1288) and project terms (W5446).
Resolve disputes using the captured evidence (weight tickets, sign-off W5455, photos); issue credit notes per policy (VS-16 W287).
Monitor AR aging; pursue collections per the standard VS-16 process; coordinate credit risk (VS-68) for B2B.
Feed dispute root-causes into pricing/service improvement (W5464) and revenue assurance (VS-118).

fields.Trigger: Monthly/quarterly analytics cycle; ESG reporting (VS-25); B2B customer KPI (W5446)
fields.Volume: 1 diversion/composition analytics view across the program

workflows.name: Diversion Rate, Stream Composition & Circular-Economy Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-diversion-rate computation from manifest/weight data; stream-composition visualization; circular-value modeling.
Controls: - CTL-805 (ensure controlled execution — Diversion, Disposal, Settlement & Site Cleanup Analytics (PA-191.3).)
- operational: diversion rate reported monthly with manifest-backed evidence.
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (ESG), VS-179 (EPR/circular), VS-73 (circular economy), VS-28 (analytics), W5453 (routing), W5460 (ESG reporting)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Diversion-underperformance risk**: actual diversion falls short of customer/ESG commitments, damaging B2B relationships and ESG ratings; mitigated by active routing optimization and new partnerships.
- **Data-quality risk**: incomplete manifests/weights distort diversion reporting; mitigated by the no-manifest-no-dispatch gate (W5452) and certified weights (W5451).
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (VS-28); weight/manifest data (W5451/W5452); routing/destination data (W5453); ESG platform (VS-25); settlement/recovery data (W5457).

steps.activity: Compute diversion rate (diverted-to-recovery ÷ total C&D generated) by job, region, channel, and customer; track against target.
Analyze stream composition (wood/drywall/masonry/metals/packaging/residuals) to identify high-volume streams for new diversion partnerships.
Quantify circular-economy value: scrap-metal recovery, reprocessor credits, biomass/aggregate reuse — vs landfill tip-fee avoided.
Benchmark diversion rate vs. industry/ESG expectations and B2B customer commitments (W5446).
Recommend improvements (new recycler partnership, on-site crushing, source-reduction) feeding W5453 routing and W5464 strategy.

fields.Frequency: Annual ESG report; periodic rater requests
fields.Participants: Services Analytics (W5459), Compliance (VS-22), ESG/IR (VS-173), Services Manager
fields.Trigger: ESG reporting cycle (VS-25); B2B customer sustainability disclosure; investor/ESG-rater request (VS-173)
fields.Volume: 1 ESG/diversion/decarbonization data feed from the program

Automation Opportunity: - Metric auto-computation from manifest data; framework-aligned auto-mapping; audit-trail automation.
Controls: - CTL-805 (ensure controlled execution — Diversion, Disposal, Settlement & Site Cleanup Analytics (PA-191.3).)
- operational: every diversion/emission claim ties to manifest evidence.
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (ESG/GHG), VS-179 (EPR/circular), VS-173 (investor/ESG-rater), VS-21.3 (audit), W5459 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unverifiable-ESG-claim risk**: a diversion/avoided-emission claim that doesn't tie to manifest evidence risks greenwashing exposure and audit qualification; mitigated by manifest-backed evidence and audit-trail.
- **Double-counting risk**: recovery credits claimed both as diversion and as scope-3 reduction; mitigated by clear accounting boundaries (VS-25).
System Touchpoints: - ESG/sustainability platform (VS-25); analytics (VS-28); manifest/weight evidence (W5451/W5452); GHG accounting (VS-25 W192); investor reporting (VS-173).
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 weeks/annual ESG report cycle for the program's contribution; ad-hoc per rater/customer request.

steps.activity: Translate program diversion/recovery data (W5459) into ESG metrics: tons diverted, % diversion, materials recovered, landfill-avoided, scope-3 circularity.
Map to reporting frameworks (GRI 306 Waste, IRIS+ waste metrics, SASB, potential ISSB S2) and BuildRight's ESG report structure (VS-25).
Compute avoided emissions (landfill methane avoidance, material-recovery credits) feeding decarbonization accounting (VS-25 W192/W3466).
Support B2B customer sustainability disclosure requests (W5446 SLA) and ESG-rater/investor queries (VS-173) with audited data.
Retain evidence for ESG assurance/audit (VS-21.3) and ensure data ties back to manifests/weights (W5451/W5452).

fields.Frequency: Monthly performance; quarterly B2B SLA review

fields.Trigger: Monthly performance cycle; service-quality assurance (VS-146); SLA review (W5446)

workflows.name: Service Performance, SLA & Customer Satisfaction Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - KPI auto-computation from dispatch/work-order data; survey/NPS integration; variance auto-alerts.
Controls: - CTL-805 (ensure controlled execution — Diversion, Disposal, Settlement & Site Cleanup Analytics (PA-191.3).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-146 (service QA), VS-13 (CX/survey), VS-177 (field ops), VS-124/VS-19.4 (training), VS-17/VS-33 (P&L)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Silent-dissatisfaction risk**: customers don't complain but churn / don't re-attach cleanup; mitigated by post-service survey and VS-146 service QA.
- **Estimate-accuracy-decay risk**: estimate-to-actuals variance creeps up over time, eroding margin; mitigated by variance monitoring feeding pricing/estimation refresh (W5442/W5441).
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (VS-28); survey/CX (VS-13/VS-146); dispatch/telematics (W5444/VS-06); field ops (VS-177); services P&L (VS-17/VS-33).

steps.activity: Track operational KPIs: on-time arrival, job cycle time, estimate-to-actuals variance, first-time-completion, punch-list rate, and safety incidents (VS-24).
Track customer satisfaction (post-service survey W5455, complaint rate VS-13, NPS) and feed VS-146 service-quality assurance.
Review B2B project SLA compliance (W5446) — hauling cycle, diversion target, response time — with the account team (VS-107).
Diagnose underperformers (region/crew/channel) and feed field coaching (VS-177) and crew training (VS-124/VS-19.4).
Report performance into the services P&L (VS-17/VS-33) and program strategy (W5464).

fields.Participants: VS-67 vendor scorecard, TPRM (VS-161), Dispatch (W5444), Finance (VS-15)
fields.Trigger: Quarterly vendor review; capacity expansion; cost-reduction initiative

Automation Opportunity: - Vendor-scorecard auto-computation; total-cost-to-serve modeling; backhaul/clustering opportunity detection.
Controls: - CTL-21: scorecard/cost accuracy; CTL-09 (vendor concentration monitoring); CTL-37 (TPRM); operational: total-cost-to-serve (not headline rate) drives vendor decisions.
Cross-references: - links to VS-110 (freight procurement), VS-67 (vendor scorecard), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-06/VS-61 (fleet/cost), W5444 (dispatch)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-lock-in risk**: a region dependent on a single hauler/disposer faces price escalation or service failure; mitigated by multi-vendor strategy and capacity monitoring.
- **Hidden-cost risk**: low headline haul rate offset by demurrage, rejection, and long-haul surcharges erodes the deal; mitigated by total-cost-to-serve scorecarding.
System Touchpoints: - Vendor scorecard (VS-67); freight procurement (VS-110); TPRM (VS-161); dispatch/telematics (W5444/VS-06); cost analytics (VS-28/VS-61).

steps.activity: Maintain a vendor scorecard (haulers/disposers/recyclers): on-time pickup, manifest accuracy, accreditation currency, contamination-rejection rate, cost/cu.m., recovery-credit delivery.
Compute cost-to-serve by region/channel/stream (crew + container + haul + disposal − recovery) and identify cost-reduction levers.
Optimize hauling: route clustering (W5444), backhaul opportunities, container-fleet utilization, and capacity-balancing across vendors.
Manage vendor performance/issues/exit via VS-110 freight and VS-161 TPRM; consolidate spend for better rates where scale allows.
Feed cost-to-serve into pricing health (W5464) and the vendor-strategy/TPRM governance.

workflows.name: DENR/LGU Periodic Waste Reporting & Permit Evidence

Automation Opportunity: - Manifest-to-report auto-aggregation; compliance-calendar integration (VS-166); permit-expiry auto-alert.
Controls: - CTL-805 (ensure controlled execution — Diversion, Disposal, Settlement & Site Cleanup Analytics (PA-191.3).)
- operational: compliance calendar drives all periodic submissions.
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-166 (license portfolio), VS-88 (records), VS-21.3 (audit), VS-100 (legal/regulatory change)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reporting-gap risk**: missed/inaccurate periodic DENR/LGU waste reports trigger compliance findings/penalties; mitigated by a compliance calendar (VS-166) and aggregated manifest data.
- **Permit-lapse risk**: a lapsed transporter/disposer accreditation or LGU placement permit halts operations; mitigated by the VS-166 license-portfolio monitoring.
System Touchpoints: - Manifest system (W5452); DENR/LGU reporting; license-portfolio (VS-166); records retention (VS-88); audit evidence (VS-21.3).

steps.activity: Aggregate manifest/disposal/ diversion data (W5452/W5453/W5459) into the DENR/LGU periodic waste-reporting format (RA 9003/RA 6969 where applicable).
Submit to DENR-EMB / LGU-ENRO per schedule and retain acknowledgement.
Maintain transporter/disposer accreditation evidence (W5447) and the LGU placement-permit register (W5445) in the VS-166 license portfolio.
Support audit (VS-21.3) with manifest/permit/weight-ticket evidence; retain per BIR/DENR record-retention (VS-88).
Monitor regulatory change (new C&D diversion mandates, LGU ordinances) and update the program (W5464) accordingly.

fields.Participants: Services Manager, Pricing (VS-01.2), Merchandising (VS-01), Finance (VS-17/VS-33), Strategy (VS-33)
fields.Trigger: Annual strategy cycle; new channel/market entry; capacity/demand imbalance; pricing-margin review

workflows.name: Program Strategy, Pricing Health & Capacity Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Demand forecast from install/build pipeline; capacity-vs-demand gap modeling; margin auto-monitoring.
Controls: - CTL-805: ensure controlled execution — Diversion, Disposal, Settlement & Site Cleanup Analytics (PA-191.3).) — strategy/investment approval; CTL-21 (pricing/capacity analysis; CTL-37 (ESG/strategic alignment); operational: program strategy reviewed annually against install/build and ESG goals.
Cross-references: - links to VS-12/VS-66/VS-143/VS-70 (install/build channels), VS-107 (B2B), VS-25/VS-179 (ESG/circular), VS-33 (strategy), VS-112 (PMO), W5441 (catalog), W5462 (cost/vendor)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Strategic-drift risk**: the program runs as a cost center / afterthought rather than a deliberate attach-and-ESG lever; mitigated by annual strategy review tying it to install/build and ESG goals.
- **Capacity-shortfall risk**: install/build growth outpaces cleanup capacity, degrading attach and customer experience; mitigated by capacity planning linked to the install/build forecast.
System Touchpoints: - Strategy/planning (VS-33); services P&L (VS-17); pricing (VS-01.2/VS-101); analytics (VS-28); PMO (VS-112).

steps.activity: Review the program's strategic role: attach lever for install/build sales, B2B differentiation (VS-107), ESG/circular positioning (VS-25/VS-179), and contribution to services P&L.
Assess pricing health: realized margin per service/region, estimate-to-actuals variance (W5461), cost-to-serve trends (W5462), and recovery-credit contribution; adjust the catalog (W5441).
Plan capacity: crew/container/haul-vendor capacity vs. forecast demand from install/build volume and B2B project pipeline (VS-11/VS-66); identify gaps.
Identify growth/reduction: extend to new channels/regions, add value (on-site crushing, source-reduction consulting), or scale back unprofitable segments.
Approve investment/changes through the services/PMO governance (VS-112) and corporate planning (VS-33); brief leadership.
